chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic:
'Or do they envy the people for what God has given them of His Grace?'
So he said: 'O Abu al-Sabbah! We, by God, are the envied people.'

key_terms.النَّاسُ الْمَحْسُودُونَ: The envied people — the Ahl al-Bayt, who are envied for their divinely bestowed authority and spiritual gifts
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God
key_terms.فَضْلِهِ: His Grace — the divine favors, including the imamate and special knowledge, granted to the Prophet's household
key_terms.وَاللَّهِ: By God — a strong oath emphasizing the certainty of the declaration

ai.seo_question: Who are 'the envied people' mentioned in Quran 4:54 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: The narrator Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the interpretation of Quran 4:54, wherein God speaks of 'the people' who are envied for the divine blessings given to them. The Imam declares emphatically — swearing by God — that the Ahl al-Bayt (the household of the Prophet) are precisely 'the envied people' referenced in the verse. This hadith is part of a chapter establishing the special divine status and authority (wilayah) of the Imams as the Masters of Command (Wali al-Amr), and their being objects of envy corresponds to the spiritual gifts and authority bestowed upon them.
